Games · Highlights · How it works · Quick start · What works · Controls · Building and usage · Tests · Contributing

# XCL – Xbox Series X|S → Windows compatibility layer XCL is a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) games you own on a Windows PC - in the spirit of Wine/Proton. There is no CPU emulation: the game's x64 code runs natively, and XCL provides its own, independently written implementations of the console system libraries the PC does not have (`kernelx.dll`, XGameRuntime, `d3d12_xs.dll`, …). The console's GPU code (RDNA2 machine code) is recompiled into PC shaders (HLSL → DXIL). > [!IMPORTANT] > XCL works only on unpacked game files you already own. It does not download, decrypt or unpack game packages (XVC / MSIXVC) and contains nothing for circumventing DRM. The repository holds no code, headers or binaries from the console SDK, no keys and no game data; the Windows components XCL relies on (XGameRuntime, XAudio2, D3D12, DXC) come from your own system or the public Windows SDK and are not distributed with XCL.

## Games

| Game | State | What works | Limits | |---|---|---|---| | **Minecraft Preview**
`Microsoft.MinecraftBeta` 1.18.3064.0 | ✅ playable | fully playable | – | | **Unicorn Overlord**
`SEGAofAmericaInc.Pa253b0c1Y` 1.0.0.6 | ✅ playable | fully playable | – | | **Fortnite**
`436609B6.FortniteClient` 2.0.1461.7919 | ✅ works | works fully, as far as the game allows without its online services | the game itself is online-only (multiplayer servers) | | **XDefiant**
`Ubisoft.XDefiant-Game` 1.0.0.186 | ✅ works | works fully, as far as the game allows without its servers | the game's own servers have been shut down | | **A newer retail game** | 🚧 **≈ 60 %**
estimate | starts in ~4 s, runs at a steady 30 fps without a crash, shows its menus and goes on past the first one to its settings; fits a 32 GB machine (~15 GB committed in the menus). With the NVIDIA integration branch ([#2057](https://github.com/xcl-dev/xcl/pull/2057)) it goes on into its 3D world: **~5 fps there** on an RTX 5090 (14 fps on average over a whole 5-minute run, its menus and loading included) | not playable yet: the picture of the world is incomplete (its minimap and other mesh pipelines are refused), and it does not keep running there for long | ## Highlights

No CPU emulation – the game's x64 code runs natively, in the spirit of Wine / Proton.

100 % of a retail game's shaders translate – all 26 698 RDNA2 programs (26 503 records) of its shader pack become HLSL; random samples compile to DXIL with 0 errors.

The game's own console DLLs run on the PC – its Bink 2 video codec decodes the game's movies, its ray-tracing BVH builder builds acceleration structures on a PC GPU, the AMD FSR 4 console upscaler runs a whole frame on a PC GPU, the GDK HTTP library initialises.

Console texture layouts – the archive test reads and detiles all 912 entries in the retail sample, including cubemaps and volume textures.

The console's storage queues – DirectStorage with file and memory sources, zlib and BCPack (BC1, BC3 – BC7).

370+ automated tests, including GPU tests that compare translated shaders against expected results instruction by instruction.
## How it works

The game's code runs on the CPU as it is; each call into a console library lands in XCL's own implementation of it, and each shader is translated once and cached. The details: [`docs/specs/2026-11-20-xcl-design.md`](docs/specs/2026-11-20-xcl-design.md), status and measurements: [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md). ## Quick start 1. **Build** – Windows 10 / 11 x64, Rust and the Windows SDK ([all requirements](#building-and-usage)): ```powershell cargo build --release --workspace ``` 2. **Look at your game** – its unpacked files, the folder that holds `MicrosoftGame.config`: ```powershell target\release\xcl.exe inspect D:\Game\game.exe ``` 3. **Run it** – or open `xcl.exe` from Explorer and choose the game: ```powershell target\release\xcl.exe run D:\Game ``` A gamepad is recommended ([Controls](#controls)). The game folder is never modified.

## What works ✅ done and verified
Running the game's code – PE loader, kernelx, Memory, File system, DirectStorage | Feature | State | What it does | Verified by | |---|---|---|---| | **PE loader** | ✅ | relocations, imports by name / ordinal / delay-load, TLS callbacks, exception tables, game DLLs, data-driven import routing (HLE / Windows / stub) | the game's 16 console DLLs load with 0 unresolved imports | | **kernelx** | ✅ | title memory (budget from MicrosoftGame.Config, physical pages), threads on the PC's processors, modules, OS / console info | unit + end-to-end tests | | **Memory** | ✅ | title graphics memory shared by CPU and GPU without copies, up to 16 GB (4 GiB windows) | GPU tests: loads, stores and atomics across windows | | **File system** | ✅ | console paths (`GAME:`, `G:`, `D:` …) → the game folder; writes go to an overlay, the game folder is never modified; the console's drives: `S:\` (persistent local storage) and `T:\` (temp) in the title's data folder; free disk space answered for console paths | end-to-end: the test title's folder stays byte-identical; PLS and free space through the real call path | | **DirectStorage** | ✅ | the console's DirectStorage queues: file and memory sources, zlib, and BCPack – the console's texture compression – for BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7 (BC2 and the hardware swizzle are refused) | unit tests on synthetic streams; retail BCPack chunks of all six modes byte-identical with a reference decoder (`XCL_SAMPLE_BCPACK`) |
System services – XGameRuntime, Input, Audio | Feature | State | What it does | Verified by | |---|---|---|---| | **XGameRuntime** | ✅ | the GDK thunk protocol real titles use, laid out from a table of all 396 GDK runtime functions; offline XUser, XGameSave, persistent local storage, XPackage, XGame (title id), XSystem – the title sees an Xbox Series X / S; task queues, async, networking and dialogs through the PC's XGameRuntime | the game's libHttpClient initialises; users, saves and storage through the real call path; slot layout cross-checked against the game's own thunks | | **Input** | ✅ | GameInput: one gamepad – the PC's XInput controller or a PlayStation controller, and keyboard and mouse as a gamepad (see [Controls](#controls)) | unit tests; an Xbox controller in Minecraft; a DualShock 4 (USB) | | **Audio** | ✅ | XAudio2 → system XAudio2.9 (PCM / float voices; Opus 0x704F decoded via `MSOpusDecoder.dll`; XMA1 / XMA2 decoded in pure Rust) | unit + end-to-end tests |
Graphics – Shader recompiler, Pipelines, D3D12.X compute, D3D12.X graphics, Textures, Ray tracing, Upscaling | Feature | State | What it does | Verified by | |---|---|---|---| | **Shader recompiler** | ✅ | RDNA2 → HLSL → DXIL: VS, PS, CS, mesh (NGG), GS; atomics, LDS, scratch, images, samplers incl. static ones, wave ops, ray-tracing instructions; structured control flow; parallel DXC, disk cache | 26 698 / 26 698 programs of the retail pack; 0 DXC errors on random samples; per-instruction GPU tests | | **Pipelines** | ✅ | PSOs from console shaders: VS+PS, CS, MS+PS, VS+GS+PS; root signature with the shaders' static samplers; non-blocking creation – a pipeline whose shaders are not compiled yet gets a stand-in at once and is built in the background | GPU tests drawing the game's own VS / PS pairs, also built in the background | | **D3D12.X compute** | ✅ | console device slots, console descriptor heaps (T# / V# / S#), buffers at their console addresses, compute command lists recorded in the console format and replayed (tables, barriers, clears, copies) | the game's BVH builder and FSR 4 record and run through XCL | | **D3D12.X graphics** | ✅ | device, resources and heaps (also placed in title memory), pipelines; the title's graphics command lists – draws, indirect draws, graphics root arguments, barriers, copies, clears – and command lists recorded by console code, replayed; `PresentX` and frame pacing into an XCL window | Minecraft Preview plays its worlds (millions of draws, none skipped); Fortnite and XDefiant draw their screens | | **Textures** | ✅ | GFX10 tiling (all 14 2D swizzle modes, the 6 3D thick modes, linear), mip chains with mip tail, arrays, cubes and 3D textures → PC textures | 912 / 912 entries detiled in the tested retail archive; GPU upload bit exact in test fixtures | | **Ray tracing** | ✅ | BLAS / TLAS built on the GPU by the game's own XboxBvhBuilder; RDNA2 BVH node format; BVH intersection instructions emulated in shaders | GPU traversal = brute force reference; the game's builder output checked on the GPU | | **Upscaling** | ✅ | the game's AMD FSR 4 console DLL (`amd_fidelityfx_upscaler_xbox.dll`): context, the 29 pipelines in the console driver's own container (FSPX) translated, a frame's 20 passes recorded and run on the GPU | end-to-end with the real DLL: a 1280×720 → 1920×1080 frame on an RX 9070, the input's gradient in the output | Far-jump address calculations are resolved to fixed targets only when branches enter at the start of the calculation. An entry partway through it keeps the jump indirect and subject to the recompiler's existing indirect-branch limits.
Media and tools – Video, Tools | Feature | State | What it does | Verified by | |---|---|---|---| | **Video** | ✅ | the game's Bink 2 console DLL decodes its movies (720p / 1080p) on the CPU; the game's own YUV → RGB display shaders (`PS_Bink…` in its pack) translate like any other. Bink's GPU-assisted mode needs no Bink-specific support: its compute shaders ship with the game and go through the recompiler too (no game seen using it yet) | a game movie decodes frame by frame, picture checked | | **Tools** | ✅ | `xcl inspect`, `xcl run`, `xcl disasm` (RDNA2, console shader containers), `xcl shaders` (pack statistics, recompile / compile runs), `xcl rpf` | – |
## Controls A **gamepad is recommended**: console games are made for one, and their menus and controls expect it. - **Gamepad:** any controller Windows sees through XInput (Xbox controllers, wired or wireless) is the game's gamepad – buttons, sticks, triggers and rumble. It can be plugged in or out while the game runs. GameInput keeps half a second of recent state changes so titles can read inputs between frames. - **PlayStation controllers** (DualShock 4 wired or over Bluetooth, DualSense wired) are the gamepad when no XInput controller is connected – buttons, sticks and triggers, no rumble or light bar. `XCL_PLAYSTATION_PAD=0` turns this off. - **Keyboard and mouse** work too, as a gamepad: WASD the left stick, the mouse the right stick, mouse buttons the triggers, the wheel the bumpers, Enter / Space A, Escape / Backspace B, arrows the D-pad, E / Q Y / X, Shift / Ctrl the stick clicks, Tab View, P Menu. `keyboard_mouse` and `mouse_sensitivity` in the game's `xcl.toml` turn it off or change the mouse speed. A gamepad and the keyboard / mouse can be used together. To override keyboard and mouse controls for one title, add an optional table to its `xcl.toml`. For example, use arrow keys for the left stick, clear the arrow-key D-pad bindings, and swap the mouse buttons: ```toml [input_profile] move_up = ["up"] move_left = ["left"] move_down = ["down"] move_right = ["right"] dpad_up = [] dpad_left = [] dpad_down = [] dpad_right = [] left_trigger = ["mouse_left"] right_trigger = ["mouse_right"] ``` Omitted entries use the built-in bindings. An empty list clears a binding. The output names are `move_up`, `move_left`, `move_down`, `move_right`, `a`, `b`, `x`, `y`, the four `dpad_*` directions, `view`, `menu`, `left_bumper`, `right_bumper`, `left_stick`, `right_stick`, `left_trigger`, and `right_trigger`. Each accepts a list of alternative inputs. Input names include `a` through `z`, `digit0` through `digit9`, `num0` through `num9`, `f1` through `f12`, `left_shift`, `right_ctrl`, `right_alt`, `mouse_middle`, `mouse_x1`, and `mouse_x2`. The `physical_q`, `physical_w`, `physical_e`, `physical_a`, `physical_s`, and `physical_d` inputs follow the positions used by the default layout. Set `wheel_up` and `wheel_down` to a single gamepad button name such as `right_bumper` or `y`, or to `unbound`. Restart the title to apply changes. ## Building and usage Windows 10/11 x64, Rust (`stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`), the Windows SDK (DXC: `dxcompiler.dll` and `dxil.dll`, looked up in `Windows Kits\10\bin\\x64`, next to `xcl.exe` or in `%XCL_DXC_DIR%`), a D3D12 GPU with Shader Model 6.6 and mesh shaders, and the system XGameRuntime (`System32\xgameruntime.dll`, part of Windows / Gaming Services). On **Windows 10** (22H2 KB5029331+), inbox `D3D12Core.dll` stops at SM 6.5; place the Microsoft D3D12 Agility SDK (`D3D12Core.dll`, plus `d3d12SDKLayers.dll` if using `XCL_D3D12_DEBUG=1`) in a `D3D12\` folder next to `xcl.exe`, directly next to `xcl.exe`, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\XCL\D3D12\`, or point `%XCL_D3D12_DIR%` at it (for `cargo test`, use `%LOCALAPPDATA%\XCL\D3D12\` or `%XCL_D3D12_DIR%`). - **DXC:** 1.8 or newer is recommended, from the [DirectXShaderCompiler releases](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/releases): unpack one and point `XCL_DXC_DIR` at its `bin\x64`. A Windows SDK may hold an older one (the same `10.0.26100.0` folder has DXC 1.7.2308 or 1.8.2502, depending on the SDK's revision). DXC 1.7's DXIL was 2–2.7 times the size of 1.9's for translated compute programs and took an NVIDIA driver 1.4–2.2 times as long to build pipelines from ([#156](https://github.com/ivall/xcl/issues/156)). `xcl run` prints the DXC it loaded, and `report.json` has it under `dxc`. A compute program with many memory-window accesses is compiled as two libraries, the program and its accessors, and linked, which is much faster for DXC (`XCL_LINK_MEM=0` turns it off); the linker needs DXC 1.8 or newer. With an older one the first attempt fails, `xcl.log` says so, and every program is compiled whole after that. - **GPU:** developed on AMD RDNA4. The console's geometry and NGG programs run as a compute pass plus a mesh pass, so a GPU without mesh shaders draws none of them. On GPUs with 32-lane waves only (NVIDIA) console wave64 compute, geometry and mesh programs run as two 32-lane halves that exchange masks and lane values ([`docs/wave64-on-wave32.md`](docs/wave64-on-wave32.md)) – slower than 64-lane waves, most for groups of several waves; wave64 vertex and pixel shaders that read lanes 32–63 can still differ there. With `XCL_DIRECT_DXIL=1` and `XCL_PER_LANE=1`, compute groups made up of complete native waves can use the per-lane form for branches on whole-wave masks. Test results on other GPUs: [#42](https://github.com/ivall/xcl/issues/42). ```powershell cargo build --release --workspace # target\release\xcl.exe xcl inspect D:\Game\game.exe # the game's imports and what XCL has for them xcl run D:\Game [-- game arguments] # run xcl disasm [--hex] # RDNA2 disassembler (console containers too) xcl shaders D:\data\shaders.rpf --top 50 # pack statistics; --recomp / --compile N xcl shaders D:\data\shaders.rpf --precompile --only cs --pipelines # build compute pipelines and save driver blobs for the next run xcl shaders D:\data\shaders.rpf --precompile --only cs --pipelines --used-only # only the compute pipelines an earlier run of the title used xcl shaders D:\data\shaders.rpf --export-hlsl out --record-hash HEX # exact compute HLSL for investigation xcl shaders D:\data\shaders.rpf --measure-pso HEX --repeat 3 # cold driver PSO timing (cache disabled) xcl rpf D:\data\shaders.rpf --extract NAME --out folder ```
Switches, caches, logs and the files XCL writes - When a game folder contains a `shaders.rpf` shader pack or loose `.dxbc` files under `shaders/`, XCL shows shader preparation in the game window before executing title code. The same window then presents the game. The percentage counts processed records. The timer counts seconds since one finished (or preparation started); five seconds without progress counts as a stall, and the window shows when the last one ended. XCL prepares supported shader stages and compute pipelines, including split pieces and their whole fallback. Graphics pipelines that need state supplied by the title are created during play. Later launches reuse matching cache entries. Closing the window cancels the launch. A compiler or driver failure stops it and reports the cause. Null-renderer runs skip shader preparation. With presentation disabled, the gate runs without a window. `XCL_PREPARE=0` leaves the preparation out: the game starts at once and builds the shaders it uses as it goes (it stands still while they build). - For compute shaders that XCL can split, the runtime first tries the saved driver blob for the whole shader. A usable blob lets the GPU run it in one dispatch. If the blob is missing or the driver rejects it, XCL builds the split pieces. - **`--pipelines` size cap**: a compute program whose DXIL is over 8 MiB and that has no saved blob is left to the runtime instead of being compiled in the pass — those compiles take tens of minutes and gigabytes and stopped the pass on the biggest programs. `XCL_PIPELINE_MAX_KB` sets the cap in KiB (0 turns it off). - **Without a command line** (xcl.exe opened from Explorer) XCL shows a small menu: *Choose a game…* (pick its exe or `MicrosoftGame.config`) or *Run again* (the last one). On an error the window stays open until Enter. - XCL works on **unpacked** game files you own; it contains nothing for decrypting or circumventing DRM. - **The game folder is never modified** – writes go to the overlay. - **Switches for how a title runs** (set them in the environment of `xcl run`): - `XCL_SKIP_BINK`: skips the Bink 2 movies of a title that ships a `bink2*.dll` (its logos and intros), by taking them straight to their last frame without decoding. Off when unset or `0`, `off`, `false` or `no`; `all` also skips looping movies; any other value (`1`, `intro` …) skips the ones that do not loop. - `XCL_MUTE_TTS`: the title gets no Windows speech synthesis: its XAccessibility requests are answered by XCL's own object, which has closed captions and high contrast only. Off by default; any value except empty, `0`, `off` or `false` (in any case) turns it on. - `XCL_FRAME_INTERVAL_US`: changes the console frame clock. Unset, the title's own frame interval (`SetFrameIntervalX`) is kept. `0`, `off` or `uncapped` removes the cap, so `WaitFrameEventX` returns at once with a fresh token. A number of microseconds is an upper bound on the interval, never below 1000: `8333` for 120 Hz, `4167` for 240 Hz. - `XCL_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` and `XCL_GPU_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, for diagnostics: the longest XCL waits for a `Wait32BitValueX` / `Wait64BitValueX` that nothing satisfies (2000 ms) and the watchdog for a GPU queue wait (5000 ms). A value that is not a number above 0 keeps the default. - Translated shaders are reused across XCL rebuilds when the translator sources and DXC toolchain are unchanged; `XCL_TRANSLATED_CACHE=0` disables that disk cache. - Direct compute dispatches can split large programs into pipelines built in parallel. `XCL_DIRECT_SPLIT_INSTRUCTIONS` sets the target instructions per piece (default 12500, zero disables splitting). Loops stay in one piece. A strongly connected component over the target gets its own piece, up to four times the target. Larger components and indirect dispatches use the whole pipeline. - Huge pipelines (translated DXIL of `XCL_HUGE_PSO_BYTES` or more, default 262144) built on the background `xcl-pso*` workers take turns in the driver's compiler: `XCL_HUGE_PSO_CONCURRENCY` at once (default 1, maximum 64). Pipelines of 4 MiB or more use a separate one-wide lane so they cannot occupy the ordinary huge-pipeline slot; one of them can therefore run next to the ordinary ones, and each gated compile starts only with 3 GB of commit free. Smaller pipelines and those a game thread waits for never wait. `xcl.log` shows each huge one as a numbered `driver compile start #K` / `driver compile finish #K: … PSO, N B DXIL, M ms` pair (compute ones with `record HASH`, the console record's hash that `--measure-pso` and `--export-hlsl --record-hash` take), with whether it was gated and how long it waited; `XCL_PSO_TRACE=1` logs every driver compile. A huge compute program the driver refuses is logged with the driver's verdict (`the driver refused the compute PSO of record HASH … with 0x…`): its dispatches are skipped. - With `XCL_DRED=1`, a D3D12 device removal logs GPU breadcrumbs in `xcl.log`. XCL examines up to 4,096 command lists and reports up to 64 unfinished lists, starting with those on which the GPU completed at least one operation. For each, it names the translated pipeline bound at the last operation DRED saw complete and those bound after it, by their console shaders' hashes (`cs`, `vs` / `ps`, `ms` / `ps`, `vs` / `gs` / `ps`). - `XCL_DSTORAGE_PARALLEL_DECOMPRESS=1` enables parallel CPU decompression for file-backed zlib requests with virtual destinations. Defaults: four workers and a shared 32 MiB staging budget (`XCL_DSTORAGE_WORKERS`, `XCL_DSTORAGE_MEMORY_BUDGET_MIB`). Requests retire in queue order. - Every run writes `report.json` (called stubs, unknown D3D12.X slots and interfaces, XGameRuntime classes asked for, shader statistics, audio formats, crash). `d3d12.presents` counts presentations, not visible content. With `XCL_FRAME_DUMP=N` (`N > 1`), the existing optional frame dumps also set `d3d12.last_frame_dump`: the latest sampled frame's zero-based index, source dimensions, DXGI format, sample step, sample count and `non_dark_samples` (decoded 8-bit R+G+B > 30). The field is `null` until a frame is sampled; `non_dark_samples` is `null` if its format cannot be decoded. Intermediate render-target dumps do not update it. Sampling uses every fourth pixel in each direction (`XCL_FRAME_DUMP_FULL=1`: every pixel). A coarse sample can miss detail; a non-dark sample does not establish correct rendering or gameplay. - **Diagnostics for a bug report** (all off by default; set them in the environment of `xcl run`): - `XCL_RUN_SECONDS=n`: the title ends itself after `n` seconds, with the GPU drained and `xcl.log` and `report.json` written, so a run of a fixed length can be attached. A value that is not a whole number is ignored. - `XCL_ACTIVITY=1` (any value turns it on): every 2 seconds `xcl.log` gets an `activity (2 s)` line with what the title did in that time (presents, submits, draws, dispatches, frame-event waits, DirectStorage requests), and a `memory:` line with the process's commit and the video memory in use. Where the lines stop changing is where the title stopped. - `XCL_THREAD_DUMP_AT=s1,s2,…`: at each of those seconds after the start, the state of every thread of the title goes into `xcl.log`, for a title that stalls. - `XCL_TRACE_FAULTS=1` (any value): the first 32 access violations are logged as they are raised (read, write or execute, the address, some registers and the callers on the stack), before the title's own handlers see them – for a title whose crash filter ends the process without a trace. - `XCL_TRACE_MEM=1` (any value turns it on): the title's memory allocations of 64 KiB or more are logged, the first 60 (`XCL_TRACE_MEM=n` with `n > 1`: the first `n`). The same variable also logs XCL's own allocations of 1 MB or more in the title's committed memory window, and the ones that fail. - `XCL_TRACE_IMPORTS`: logs the arguments and the result of every call of the imports it names. A comma-separated list: `1` or `hle` for every function XCL implements (also what a list with no word to add means), `all` for the system's functions too (short runs only), any other word is the start of a `dll!Function` name to add, and `-word` one to leave out; the name is the DLL's file name with its extension and case does not matter, so for example `hle,-kernelx.dll!GetTickCount,gameinput`. - `XCL_D3D12_TRACE=1` (any value): every call console code makes to a public D3D12.X method is logged with the interface and method name. Very verbose: use it for a short run. - Title data: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\XCL\\` (`%XCL_DATA_ROOT%`): `xcl.toml`, `overlay\`, `saves\`, `pls\` (the title's `S:\`), `temp\` (`T:\`), `cache\`, `logs\xcl.log`, `logs\report.json` (the previous run's: `xcl.prev.log`, `report.prev.json`). </details> ## Tests ```powershell .\scripts\test.ps1 # cargo build --workspace + cargo test --workspace ``` Unit tests, an end-to-end test with our own "console title" (`tests/testtitle`) and GPU tests (D3D12, SM 6.6; skipped without a GPU / DXC; `XCL_ADAPTER=1` or `XCL_ADAPTER=radeon` picks another adapter than the first high-performance one, for titles too). A GPU test that cannot run on the adapter (no GPU / DXC / wave64 / mesh shaders) passes too, but prints `SKIPPED <test>: <reason>`, and `scripts/test.ps1` counts them at the end; `XCL_REQUIRE_GPU=wave64` (or `mesh`, or `wave64,mesh`) makes those skips fail. Tests on real game data are opt-in through environment variables pointing at your own files – `XCL_SAMPLE_RPF` (shader pack), `XCL_SAMPLE_DLLS` (the game's console DLLs), `XCL_SAMPLE_TTPF` (an RDS5 texture archive, checked entry by entry), `XCL_SAMPLE_BCPACK` (a folder of BCPack streams `<name>.bc<mode>` with a reference decoder's blocks of each, `<name>.vic<mode>`), `XCL_SAMPLE_BK2` (a movie), `XCL_SAMPLE_BVH4`, `XCL_SAMPLE_AWC` (a sound) – described in `HANDOFF.md`; without them those tests pass without running anything (`scripts/test.ps1` lists the ones not set). No game data is part of the repository. ## Contributing Help is welcome – [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) has what a pull request needs, in short: small, one problem, tested. Test results on your GPU go to [#42](https://github.com/xcl-dev/xcl/issues/42), questions and talk to the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/xcl). <p align="center"><img src="assets/readme/divider.svg" width="100%" alt=""></p> ## Licenses **GPL-3.0-or-later** (`LICENSE`); third-party sources: `THIRD_PARTY.md` (including AMD's machine-readable ISA, AMD addrlib swizzle patterns, LLVM disassembler tests, VIctory, FFmpeg, libHttpClient headers).
